mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of instances where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in periods where UNRATE exceeds 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings for industrial firms and drags S&P 500 returns lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of both rising FEDFUNDS above 2% and CPIAUCSL above 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive momentum in housing starts (HOUST) over six consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when HOUST shows six months of consecutive increases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, which dampens consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE also rises over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below 1% for four consecutive months signals a shift toward consumption financing, which increases sensitivity to rate changes and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when RSAFS annualized falls below 1% for four months.
